claims.text: Blackfriars Bridge is a major road and pedestrian crossing over the River Thames that currently carries the A201 road.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The very first bridge on this exact site opened back in 1769 and was initially named the William Pitt Bridge.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Locals ignored the official title, instead adopting an informal name referencing a nearby Dominican priory known as the Blackfriars Monastery.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Unfortunately, that original structure suffered from very faulty workmanship and had to be completely dismantled in 1860.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The stunning replacement bridge you see today was officially opened by Queen Victoria herself on 6 November 1869.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Designed by engineer Joseph Cubitt, the current bridge spans an impressive 923 feet across five wrought iron arches.
claims.subject: self
